name: Echo 4th Gen (US)

radios.note: Zigbee hub (CSA Zigbee 3.0 certified) and Thread border router per Amazon's developer docs. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are not listed because no official page we could read states them.

matter.note: Amazon's Matter docs list Echo (2nd Gen and newer) as Matter-enabled, with Echo acting as the Matter administrator. The CSA listing for Echo (4th Gen) is Zigbee 3.0 only, so no Matter certificate for this model is confirmed.

apple_home.note: No official source shows Echo-paired Zigbee devices in Apple Home.

google_home.note: No official source shows Echo-paired Zigbee devices in Google Home.

alexa.note: Zigbee lights, plugs, in-wall switches and locks pair straight to the Echo's built-in hub and appear in Alexa.

smartthings.note: No official source shows Echo-paired Zigbee devices in SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: No official Home Assistant page shows Echo-paired devices appearing there.

hubRequired.note: The Echo itself is the hub.

localControl.note: Not confirmed for this model. Amazon's Matter docs say some connection types let Alexa control devices locally, without naming Echo models.

deviceProtocols.note: Zigbee devices pair to the built-in hub; the Thread border router (Thread 1.1) serves Matter-over-Thread devices.

matterBridge.note: Amazon's Matter docs don't name any Echo as a Matter bridge.

maxDevices.note: No limit found in the sources.

summary: The Echo (4th Gen) has a Zigbee hub built in, so Zigbee lights, plugs, in-wall switches and locks pair straight to it and appear in Alexa with no separate hub. It also acts as a Thread 1.1 border router for Matter-over-Thread devices. Google Home, Apple Home, SmartThings and Home Assistant aren't confirmed for devices paired through it.

sources.title: Connect Your Device to Alexa with Matter

caveats: The CSA listing for this model covers Zigbee 3.0 only; Matter support rests on Amazon's developer docs.
